scope: The 29 observations present before the v1.1 live SourceGrid expansion
approvalBoundary: These are evidence-backed editorial proposals. They do not approve or publish any claim.

decisions.claimSummary: A columnist relayed another outlet's prediction that Cleveland would stand pat.
decisions.rationale: A prediction is not evidence of an inquiry, offer, negotiation or team decision.

decisions.claimSummary: A deadline explainer listed possible candidates and hypothetical reasons they could move.
decisions.rationale: Useful context, but the candidate list does not establish team contact or availability.

decisions.claimSummary: Bleacher Report attributed phone activity and positional interest to James Palmer on Prime.
decisions.rationale: The attributable original broadcast segment was not independently captured, so the secondary summary remains held.

decisions.claimSummary: Google News discovery copy of the directly ingested CBS article.
decisions.rationale: Suppress the redirect copy and retain the publisher URL.

decisions.claimSummary: Analysis of whether multi-first-round-pick trades tend to work.
decisions.rationale: Analysis does not add a new transaction fact beyond official records.

decisions.claimSummary: A rolling team blog tracker linked onward to separate reports.
decisions.rationale: The tracker is not the original source for its individual rumor claims.

decisions.claimSummary: Analysts graded already recorded transactions.
decisions.rationale: Editorial grading is analysis; official transaction rows are the controlling facts.

decisions.claimSummary: CBS analysts proposed needs and potential options for all teams.
decisions.rationale: Potential options are hypothetical unless separately supported by reporting.

decisions.claimSummary: The article attributed to Jeremy Fowler that rivals saw Arizona as potentially moving Josh Sweat and identified possible fits.
decisions.rationale: Classify only as an attributable report, not an offer, negotiation or agreement; the article itself says much of the destination discussion is speculative.

decisions.claimSummary: Albert Breer reported Cleveland was checking pass-rush and blocking-tight-end options.
decisions.rationale: This supports buyer activity at position level only; it does not identify an offer or agreement.

decisions.claimSummary: ESPN ranked players who might move and discussed team fits.
decisions.rationale: A candidate ranking is analysis, not evidence that a player is available.

decisions.claimSummary: ESPN reported background on the Titans' decision after the completed Simmons trade.
decisions.rationale: Useful context, but the transaction itself is independently established by the NFL record.

decisions.claimSummary: An explainer listed the deadline, team needs and players the author thought San Francisco could target.
decisions.rationale: The target list is hypothetical and provides no evidence of contact.

decisions.claimSummary: James Boyd reported that Josh Downs requested a trade, and quoted coach Shane Steichen discussing the request.
decisions.rationale: This supports a trade request, not a completed trade, offer or agreement.

decisions.claimSummary: A Denver Post headline framed how the Broncos might approach the deadline.
decisions.rationale: No accessible original text established an inquiry, offer or negotiation.

decisions.claimSummary: ESPN analyzed whether San Francisco might remain active after acquiring Buckner.
decisions.rationale: The headline does not itself report another inquiry or offer.

decisions.claimSummary: A team-needs article identified defensive help as Detroit's priority.
decisions.rationale: Needs analysis does not establish contact with a seller.

decisions.claimSummary: Breer reported three contract-year Eagles could be had, Barkley was less likely, and Ojomo was not available.
decisions.rationale: Preserve the positive and negative availability claims together; no offer or agreement was reported.

decisions.claimSummary: CBS argued Dallas had already won the deadline after the Porter trade.
decisions.rationale: The 'won' claim is opinion; the transaction belongs in the official record.

decisions.claimSummary: Breer reported that the Chargers had shut down trade inquiries even as availability questions persisted around Mack and Johnston.
decisions.rationale: This is material negative evidence against treating speculation as active negotiations.

decisions.claimSummary: NFL.com relayed Thomas's public comments but did not report an inquiry, offer or agreement.
decisions.rationale: Publish, if approved, only as a player statement amid rumors; NFL.com's fit analysis is not team availability confirmation.

decisions.claimSummary: Google News discovery copy of the directly ingested CBS article.
decisions.rationale: Suppress the redirect copy and retain the publisher URL.

decisions.claimSummary: An injury contingency story matched the word 'available' but contained no trade claim in the headline.
decisions.rationale: Reject as a parser false positive.

decisions.claimSummary: A Sports Illustrated team-site article ranked positions Buffalo should address.
decisions.rationale: A recommendation does not establish team contact or an available player.

decisions.claimSummary: A fantasy-oriented article identified players to monitor around the deadline.
decisions.rationale: Fantasy monitoring is analysis and does not independently establish trade activity.

decisions.claimSummary: NFL.com reported Nelson's comments after the completed trade.
decisions.rationale: The interview adds context; the official transaction record controls the completed-trade fact.

decisions.claimSummary: A roundup mixed rumors, possible fits and proposed trade costs.
decisions.rationale: No accessible original evidence established a specific inquiry, offer or negotiation.

decisions.claimSummary: Breer reported how the Simmons transaction was negotiated and approved.
decisions.rationale: Preserve as original reporting context; the official transaction record controls the completed-trade fact.

decisions.claimSummary: The author proposed five trades they wanted to see.
decisions.rationale: Explicitly hypothetical ideas must not be represented as reported trade activity.
